candidate_relations.reason: Matches the benchmark diagnosis of hemangiosarcoma and the vasoformative, invasive histology.
Hemangiosarcoma is a neoplasm, but this omits vascular lineage and malignant subtype.
Hyperplasia does not represent the invasive malignant vascular tumor described.
Focal nodular hyperplasia is a hepatocellular regenerative lesion, not hemangiosarcoma.
Liver cell adenoma differs from a malignant vascular endothelial tumor.
A hepatic hemangiosarcoma is liver disease, but the label lacks neoplastic lineage and malignancy.
Hepatocellular carcinoma has hepatocyte differentiation rather than vascular endothelial differentiation.
Hepatic angiosarcoma is synonymous with hemangiosarcoma arising in the liver, as in this record.
Hepatic adenoma is not a malignant vasoformative endothelial tumor.
Hepatoblastoma is a distinct tumor lineage from hemangiosarcoma.
Embryonal sarcoma of the liver is not the vascular endothelial malignancy specified by the benchmark.
Hemangiosarcoma in this case is hepatic neoplasia, but the label omits vascular lineage and malignant subtype.
Cholangiocarcinoma is a bile duct epithelial carcinoma, not hemangiosarcoma.
Bile duct carcinoma is a distinct epithelial malignancy from the vascular sarcoma described.
Hemangioma shares vascular lineage but conflicts with the invasive, mitotically active malignant diagnosis of hemangiosarcoma.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Benign vascular tumor instead of malignant vascular sarcoma
